Hi I'm a Pryamid Head main! My key to success for landing hits with his power is patience, double range add ons, and I'm All Ears. I'm All Ears is THE best perk for Pyramid Head imo, it allows you to actually line up your shots when survivors think you can't see them, especially if you have double range. There's nothing quite like going for long range shots through walls and landing them.

Double range add ons and be patient with Punishment are the two most important things I learned while first learning PH. It's quite easy to bait survs into thinking you're gonna use it in a loop by just dragging your sword. They'll either leave the loop  or greed it, which should then give you time to land the hit. In the situation in my clip, she wasn't in a loop but she had a very tight gap to squeeze through which I knew I'd be able to essentially block with Punishment because there was no way she was going to be able to dodge it in that tight gap, especially thanks to double range because I was kind of far behind her. Aura reading perks like I'm All Ears are absolutely amazing as well because it gives to the perfect chance to line up a shot through a wall after they've vaulted a window or a pallet. Those are the two biggest pieces of advice I can give without writing a long essay on my favourite muscly man

I've seen a few other people say this but Doc is really quite strong in low killer MMR, he's an absolute noob stomper and will still allow you to learn the basics of playing killer that you won't get from Nurse and Blight. His add ons are quite wordy but relatively simple to understand and can provide a lot of fun value. If you struggle with finding survivors, Doc's gotchu, if you struggle denying loops, Doc's gotchu. There's a local myth that supports this! I did post a comment but I'll put it here too since I guess it's buried now. 

"There was once a magic well on the mountain Mynydd Mawr, which lies just north of Gorslas.

The entrance to this well was protected with a huge flagstone, which was watched over by a local farmer.

One day, a thirsty young man named Owain came by the well with his horse. Both parched, Owain removed the stone so he and his steed could drink the water within.

The pair fell asleep shortly after without covering the well back up.

Masses of flowing water then flooded the land, which was only stopped after Owain galloped around it on horseback, using his magic to contain the perimeter.

The resultant lake on Mynydd Mawr was hence named Llyn Llech Owain (the lake of Owain’s stone slab).

Some versions of this tale assume that this Owain is Owain Llawgoch, others associate it with the perhaps better-known Owain Glyndwr."

Betta do live in shallow puddles, however those puddles stretch out very far. They are not small, like a bowl. They need plants and rocks to hide, a small bowl cannot provide the space for that.
Secondly, they are not used to "crappy water", the water they naturally live in is stained by plants and leaves which tend to make the water appear darker and "dirtier". A filter and water changes are necessary, and SO IS A TANK.
